title: Replace "manuf" files with static arrays
description:
To reduce startup external file parsing replce the manuf file with
static arrays compiled into the binary.

Add 3 tables for MA-L, MA-M and MA-S. Add a fourth table to direct
a 24-bit MAC prefix (OUI) to one of these tables.

Adapt the make-manuf.py script to generate the static C data
instead of the text file.

The arrays are sorted and a binary search is performed to map
an OUI (24bit/28bit/36bit) to a short and long name.

TODO: Add back CID and IAB registries?

When we still hosted our repository ourselves (and had access to server logs) a lot of people downloaded our manuf file directly. I'm not sure how much disruption removing it will cause. We fetch the manuf file ourselves for our [OUI lookup tool](https://www.wireshark.org/tools/oui-lookup.html) but I can modify that to use manuf-data.c.

My guess is a lot of people still download it (e.g., https://www.reddit.com/r/sysadmin/comments/ar5bpa/where_do_you_get_the_freshest_ouitxt_files/ ). It might be nice to continue to provide it (even if we use the static file), or perhaps provide a flag to allow `make-manuf.py` produce the old text file instead (the latter is somewhat less work than forcing people to use git to download the old version of the script.)

I recently wrote a [Lua OUI Lookup Tool](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/Lua/Examples/OUILookup) that uses the locally-installed `manuf` file for lookups, so removing this file will render this tool completely inoperable.
These objections are a form of ossification and I can't bring myself to care about it in the least. Sorry.

My plan was to leave the files (for enterprises/services/manuf) there, but document the fact that we were no longer going to read the global ones (which hopefully would be read-only?).  A comment could also be added to that affect at the top of each file.

So for enterprises (I started there because it is much less used), I kept tools/make-enterprises.py writing to the original file, and parsed that to create the C static array.  And I like that there is a chance that someone could have grepped the resolved name, found the file, then found the IANA website in a comment at the top of the file.

This obviously does add to the size of the installation package (including entries in compiled C code and in these text files).
Personally, I think that is a good plan, @martin.r.mathieson.
We could omit the data files and add `tshark -G ...` options to generate  them if needed.

It's not ideal but I suppose it's better than nothing if there are strong objections to just including the `manuf` file with the Wireshark installation as we do today.

I guess it's safe to assume that `tshark` is also installed with every Wireshark installation.  

Of course for those interested in writing the output to a `manuf` file, the file won't necessarily be able to be written to the default installation location because that usually requires elevated privileges, so another file location will need to be chosen instead, most likely the user's "Personal configuration" folder.

Passing the torch back to you on this @martin.r.mathieson . Feel free to use this code, or not.

FWIW I'm -1 on keeping these files around just because.
With the `global_manuf_lookup()` function added in this MR writing an OUI lookup tool is like, 0.5 lines of code.
This doesn't help for OUI lookups from Lua scripts, such as the aforementioned [OUI Lookup Tool](https://wiki.wireshark.org/Lua/Examples/OUILookup).

It's incumbent upon you to fix your code or propose an enhancement that will provide a stable API for your purposes.

Internal Wireshark files are subject to change at any time. I'm sorry it inconveniences you but the project can't stay frozen because of every toy program in the wild.

I am willing to add a Lua API for MAC lookups (by address or name pattern). Should be more useful than using text only for addresses. You'll still have to rewrite your script to use this small API of course but that is trivial.

Maybe it's better to just implement an OUI Lookup Tool directly in C in Wireshark under the Tools menu?  Having that, I don't think there would be a need for Lua integration at all, and everyone could simply have OUI lookups at their fingertips without necessarily even needing internet access in order to reach https://www.wireshark.org/tools/oui-lookup.html, and without having to install a separate Lua plugin either.

Possibly `tshark` could even be modified to support it as well, or perhaps a separate dedicated binary altogether could be written and packaged with Wireshark.  But if there's no interest in any of that, then a Lua API might be useful, or I guess we could just forget the whole thing if there's no interest in it at all.

> Maybe it's better to just implement an OUI Lookup Tool directly in C in Wireshark under the Tools menu?

OK, let's do that, sounds good to me.
If no one is working on this I think it should still go through because the gains are measurable.
It is surely worth doing.  If still closed, was planning to re-open it after my upcoming holiday (so I'd be around for any discussion).

This has the effect of causing Debian Lintian, and hence the Debian package job, to fail:

"E: libwireshark0: embedded-library ieee-data [usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwireshark.so.0.0.0]"

The ieee-data package contains all the csv files; somehow this change makes Lintian think that we're statically linking this package. I think the right thing is just to override this complaint.
Seriously Debian? You're complaining about embedding information now? That's reasonable! /s
!11560 is a MR for this patently absurd complaint by lintian.
